chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram tightening the turban around his belly. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) was saying: He can tighten the money-belt in which is his expenditure (money), to be confident from it, for it is from the completion of his Hajj'.

key_terms.إحرام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What can a pilgrim in Ihram wear or carry on their waist?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the distinction between general clothing restrictions and practical necessities for the pilgrim, specifically permitting a money-belt (minqat) to secure travel expenses. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links this allowance to the perfection of Hajj, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that carrying one's livelihood is a legitimate need that does not invalidate the state of Ihram. This ruling underscores the balance between ritual purity and practical ease in Shia fiqh.
